heroHeadline: Post-Summit Tech Bifurcation Structural — CATL Claims 47.2% of China EV Battery Market as CIBF 2026 Confirms Manufacturing Infrastructure Dominance; Zero H200 Chips to China, AI Chip Talks Unresolved
heroSubtitle: The May 18 post-summit technology landscape is defined by two converging structural stories. In battery technology, CIBF 2026 post-show analysis (Car News China, May 18) confirmed that China's battery supply chain has crossed from concept demonstration to industrial-scale deployment: CATL commanded 47.2% of China's EV battery installations in April 2026 (BYD 17.1%), with production-ready 6.5-minute LFP fast-charging cells and 2,710Ah ESS Blade batteries for utility-scale grid storage in scaled delivery. The show drew 3,000+ exhibitors and 350,000+ visitors from 50+ countries across 280,000 m² — and critically, the manufacturing infrastructure below the majors (equipment makers, electrolyte specialists, separator manufacturers) displayed production-ready systems rather than prototypes, confirming that the entire battery supply chain has reached manufacturing maturity. In semiconductors and AI, Digitimes' May 18 post-summit assessment confirmed that US Trade Representative Greer stated chip export controls were 'not a major part' of the Trump-Xi talks — the AI chip deadlock continues with zero Nvidia H200 units delivered, Chinese firms redirected to Huawei Ascend (~60% domestic AI chip market), rare earth flows ~50% suppressed, and only the bilateral AI governance framework (mutual capability notification + incident sharing) as an institutionalized summit output. The post-summit verdict as of May 18: symbolic diplomatic stabilization achieved; battery manufacturing dominance and AI hardware self-sufficiency both accelerating on independent structural trajectories.
